label: lem:integral_func_at_base
title: Integral function vanishes at the base point
statement: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ and $a \in \mathbb{R}$. Define the integral function $G : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ by $G(u) = \int_a^u f(t)\,dt$. Then $G(a) = 0$.
proof: Evaluating $G$ at the base point $a$ gives $G(a) = \int_a^a f(t)\,dt = 0$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:integral_base_zero}.
